Origin: scheduled dispatch Routine firing, 2026-09-16T14:19Z (run `2026-09-16T141326-dispatch-standalone`)

Defer-reason: tangential — found mid-firing while driving record #2485 to merge; the dispatch task itself completed successfully (PR #2522 merged, #2485 closed), this is a follow-up on the infra gap observed along the way.

## Current State

This firing ran in a `gh`-absent sandbox (cloud Routine container, confirmed via `which gh` → not found). `dispatch/mcp-transport.md` documents a real, live-verified MCP bridge for `/claude-tweaks:dispatch`'s own Step 2 queue-pull path (the bridge plan, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-02-dispatch-mcp-bridge.md`, deleted `d83f0720`) — that bridge let this firing complete its queue pull, exclusion checks, and eventual build/merge entirely via GitHub MCP tools with no `gh` at all.

`bin/hooks.js reconcile --json` has no equivalent bridge. Run twice in this firing (once before queue-pull, once after the group's PR merged), both times it reported:

```json
{"skipped":[{"check":"red-tip,reap,release,archive,archive-branches,remote-prune,console","reason":"preflight-gh-absent"}]}
```

Concretely: after dispatching group [#2485] to a successful merge (PR #2522, `pr-first` integration model), the group's worktree (`.claude/worktrees/record-2485`, branch `worktree-record-2485`) and its run directory (`.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-09-16T141943-record-2485`) are exactly the kind of residue `dispatch/SKILL.md`'s Step 6 says "the reconciler reaps ... on merged-PR evidence" — but the reconciler's `reap`/`archive` checks are unconditionally skipped whenever `gh` is absent, with no MCP substitute the way queue-pull now has one. The residue is harmless (a stale worktree/run-dir, not a correctness bug) but will accumulate indefinitely across every `gh`-absent firing until either `gh` becomes available in that sandbox or a human runs the check manually.

Also observed: a second, separate gap in this same firing — `bin/resolve-blockers.js` (`work-links: native` blocked-by check) and `bin/resolve-linked-prs.js` (the `#1224` open-PR exclusion) both hard-require `gh` with no MCP path, exiting 2 and degrading dispatch's own queue-pull to "no native filtering" / "no open-PR exclusion" this run (per those scripts' own documented exit codes and `queue-pull-script.md`'s existing `||`-fallback warnings). This firing worked around the open-PR gap by manually calling `mcp__github__issue_read`'s `get` method (whose `closed_by_pull_requests` field, contrary to `mcp-transport.md`'s "no MCP tool answers this direction" claim, actually does answer it) against every queue candidate before selecting — catching that the automated top-ranked pick (#2259) already had an open PR (#2450), and that three other candidates (#2051, #2329, #1135) plus the #2267/#2268/#2269 family (natively blocked by open #2265) were likewise falsely eligible. This matches #2051's own near-miss finding for the identical gap, one firing later, with a concrete repeat.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Investigate whether `reap-merged.js` / `release-merged.js` / `archive-merged.js` / `archive-branches.js` / `remote-prune.js` / the console check can be bridged to the GitHub MCP server the same way `dispatch`'s own queue-pull was (per `_shared/github-write-transport.md`'s CRUD mapping) — or document why each cannot (following the same per-check-mapping-or-accepted-gap shape `dispatch/mcp-transport.md` already uses).
- [ ] Re-verify (or correct) `dispatch/mcp-transport.md`'s claim that "there is no MCP tool that answers the direction this check needs — issue number → its open closing PR" (#1224's own documented gap) against `mcp__github__issue_read`'s `get` method's `closed_by_pull_requests.references[].state` field, which this firing confirmed does answer exactly that direction for a single already-known issue number (batching N candidates into one call, rather than N individual `issue_read` calls, may still be the real remaining gap — clarify which).
- [ ] Either give `resolve-blockers.js` / `resolve-linked-prs.js` a real MCP path, or promote #2051's own recommended workaround (a manual per-candidate open-PR/native-blocker verification before finalizing group selection) from "this firing's improvisation" to a documented, required step in `dispatch/mcp-transport.md`'s Step 2 section — #2051 already recommends exactly this and is still open.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Either `reconcile`'s `gh`-absent preflight gains a real MCP-bridged path for at least the `reap`/`archive` checks (the ones that directly cause worktree/run-dir residue accumulation), or the accepted-gap posture is explicitly documented in `docs/reconcile-checks.md` with the residue-accumulation consequence stated plainly.
2. `dispatch/mcp-transport.md`'s #1224 section is corrected to reflect `issue_read`'s actual `closed_by_pull_requests` capability, or explains precisely why it still doesn't close the gap (e.g. batching cost at queue-pull scale).
3. `npm test` passes.

_Filed during a scheduled `/claude-tweaks:dispatch --budget 1` Routine firing (session_01HKv2ycYHcMKbCNHvqebATz)._

Origin: split from #1811's Deliverables — the code fix (#1732/#1811) lands the branchless MERGED-by-number archival, no-run-state terminal path, and consolidated escalation, but the manual one-time catch-up against the live main-checkout run-directory state was explicitly out of scope for that worktree-isolated build.
Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

#1811's Deliverables included archiving seven specific stranded run directories under `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/` in the live main-checkout state and closing #1812–#1817 as absorbed. #1812–#1817 are already closed (absorbed into #1811 on 2026-09-10). The archival itself has not happened: verified directly against the live main checkout on 2026-09-14 — all seven directories are still present under `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/` and none exist under `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/archive/`:

| Run dir | Live state (2026-09-14) |
|---|---|
| `2026-08-27T105511-record-1378-816` | present, not archived |
| `2026-08-26T225542-record-872` | present, not archived |
| `2026-08-26T195025-record-605` | present, not archived — do not touch the unrelated live `2026-09-09T101742-record-605` run |
| `2026-08-26T043405-record-1317` | present, not archived |
| `2026-08-26T042502-record-1315` | present, not archived |
| `2026-08-23T191935-record-1292` | present, not archived |
| `2026-08-22T135220-record-1179` | present, not archived |

This is a live-state operational action (running `archive-run` against the main checkout's actual pipeline directories, editing GitHub issue comments), not a code change — it cannot be performed or committed from inside a worktree-isolated build, and running it before #1732/#1811's fix reaches `main` means the fix's new branchless-MERGED and no-run-state code paths aren't even in effect yet for whichever reconciler processes these directories.

## Deliverables

- After #1732/#1811 merges to `main`, re-confirm each of the seven directories' live state (PR merged/closed status, worktree presence) against #1811's original table — state may have drifted further since 2026-09-09/2026-09-14.
- Archive each directory that is still stuck, one `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/hooks.js" archive-run --run <dir>` call per directory (per #1811's own Deliverables), OR confirm the next scheduled `reconcile` pass (now running the merged fix) auto-archived it and only verify the result — don't hand-run `archive-run` on a directory the automated sweep already cleared.
- For `2026-08-26T195025-record-605` specifically: note in the closing comment/commit that it is superseded by the live `2026-09-09T101742-record-605` run — this note is not something the automated sweep can produce on its own.
- Confirm via `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/hooks.js" reconcile --json` that none of the seven paths remain listed under `runs` once done.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All seven directories are archived (either by hand or confirmed auto-archived by the merged fix) and none appear in `reconcile --json`'s `runs` list.
- The `2026-08-26T195025-record-605` archival comment/commit names the superseding live run.
- This record closes with a comment noting which of the seven were hand-archived vs. auto-archived by the reconcile fix.

## Technical Approach

Re-confirm #1732/#1811's fix has landed on `main` first (`git log --oneline --grep="1811"`), since the branchless-MERGED and no-run-state code paths this record depends on must be live before either archival route below is trustworthy. Then, for each of the seven directories: run `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/hooks.js" reconcile --json` and check whether it has already disappeared from the `runs` list (auto-archived) — if so, just verify it now lives under `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/archive/`. ### Key Files

- `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/{the seven listed run dirs}` — moved to `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/archive/` by this record's action
- `plugin/bin/hooks.js` — the `archive-run` and `reconcile` subcommands this record invokes (no code change, invocation only)

## Gotchas

- Do not touch the unrelated live `2026-09-09T101742-record-605` run — only the older `2026-08-26T195025-record-605` directory is in scope, and the two share a record number by coincidence.

Surface: infra

## Current State
`plugin/bin/hooks.js`'s `archive-run` verb prints the result of `archiveRunDir(mainRoot, runDir)`. One reason gets a bespoke six-line recovery message, selected by `if (result.reason === 'audit-untracked')` and interpolating `result.untrackedAuditFiles`; every other refusal prints `claude-tweaks: archival refused — {reason}`. `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` produces fourteen distinct reason codes (`move-failed`, `readdir-failed`, `mkdir-failed`, `console-unresolved`, `console-never-rendered`, `tracked-entry`, `no-pr`, `no-branch`, `network-failure`, `ls-files-failed`, `gh-absent`, `close-write-failed`, `close-failed`, `audit-untracked`, plus `git-mv-failed`/`git-mv-failed-partial-revert`) as ad hoc `{ ok: false, reason, … }` literals, some with extra fields (`lastError`, `untrackedAuditFiles`) that only the dispatcher knows to read. The recovery knowledge for `audit-untracked` lives 400 lines away from the code that detects it, and a rename of the reason code in `archive-merged.js` would silently downgrade the message to the generic line — nothing pins the two together. `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js` asserts the message text (`archival refused — audit-untracked`, `sync this checkout with origin`), so the text can move but not change.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `archive-merged.js` gains one refusal constructor, `refusal(reason, { hint = null, ...extra } = {})` → `{ ok: false, reason, hint, ...extra }`, and every `{ ok: false, reason: … }` literal in the file goes through it, so each result carries a `hint` key (string or `null`) beside its reason.
- [ ] The `audit-untracked` recovery text moves verbatim from `hooks.js` into that refusal's `hint`, built where `untrackedAuditFiles` is computed; `move-failed` and the two `git-mv-failed*` refusals set `hint` from `lastError` when present; the other codes start with `hint: null` (no invented prose).
- [ ] `hooks.js`'s `archive-run` branch drops the `reason === 'audit-untracked'` match and prints `claude-tweaks: archival refused — {reason}` followed, when `result.hint` is a non-empty string, by ` — {hint}`; the exit code and the `moved:` lines are unchanged.
- [ ] A conformance test that every `reason: '…'` literal in `archive-merged.js` sits inside a `refusal(` call (a source scan), and unit cases that `refusal` always yields a `hint` key and that the `audit-untracked` result's hint names its files.
- [ ] `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js` passes unmodified (its regexes match the moved text); `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` cases that deep-equal a refusal object are updated only to include `hint: null` where they assert whole objects.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `hooks.js` contains no comparison against a specific `archive-merged.js` reason string; the `archive-run` branch reads only `ok`, `reason`, `hint`, and `movedEntries`.
2. `node bin/hooks.js archive-run` on the untracked-audit fixture prints the same `audit-untracked` sentence as today (the existing test's regexes are the proof); every other refusal prints its reason exactly as today, with a hint appended only where one was set.
3. Every refusal object `archiveRunDir` and its helpers return has a `hint` property; the source scan finds no bare `{ ok: false, reason:` literal outside `refusal`.
4. `npm test` is green.

## Technical Approach
Co-locate the story with the detector, keep the dispatcher dumb: a `hint` field is the smallest contract change that lets the next non-obvious failure ship its recovery text without a new `if` in `hooks.js`, and a constructor is what makes "every refusal has the field" a source-scannable invariant rather than a convention. Hints stay `null` for the codes whose one-line reason already says what happened (`gh-absent`, `no-pr`); writing prose for all fourteen would be the speculative work the record warns against. The `console-*` and `network-failure` codes come from `decideArchive`'s pure skip path (`{ action: 'skip', reason }`), which is a different shape consumed inside the loop, not by `hooks.js` — leave it alone and say so in the constructor's comment.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `archiveRunDir`, `archiveOrphanedMint`, `revertWorkMoves`/`revertPlainMoves`, the `audit-untracked` branch (`untrackedAuditFiles`), every `ok: false` literal.
- `plugin/bin/hooks.js` — the `archive-run` verb's refusal printing.
- `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js` — text pins (unchanged); `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` — object-shape cases.

## Gotchas
- The `audit-untracked` sentence is asserted by regex in `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js`; move it character-for-character, including the `git pull, or reconcile's own mirror-ff` clause.
- `trackArchiveResult` in the same file consumes `result.reason` and `result.lastError` for residue tracking; adding `hint` must not change what it reads, and `lastError` stays as its own field rather than being folded into `hint`.
- #1732 (classifier) and #1733 (loop extraction) touch the same file; this record touches only the refusal literals and can land before or after either, but never in parallel with them.
- Do not print hints for `dryRun` skips: `archiveMerged`'s `skipped` entries are a different consumer and the reconcile report renders them itself.

## Original request

`plugin/bin/hooks.js` has a single hardcoded `if (result.reason === 'audit-untracked')` branch that prints a bespoke multi-line recovery message, while `archive-merged.js`'s ~15 other reason codes (`mkdir-failed`, `git-mv-failed`, `ls-files-failed`, `tracked-entry`, `commit-failed`, ...) all fall through to a generic one-line message. The rich, actionable recovery text lives in the CLI dispatcher rather than co-located with the code that understands the failure, and nothing keeps a renamed/removed reason code in `archive-merged.js` in sync with this dispatcher-side string match.


Defer-reason: genuinely-larger — touches the reason-code contract across archive-merged.js's ~15 failure paths and its hooks.js dispatcher, not a localized change; found by the pre-v6.117.0 whole-branch review.

Verified-as-of: 1941be706a53ea4f6dbd5c9b4c385991cc72811e

## Current State

`skills/init/claude-md-template.md` (the installed plugin's own generator, v6.120.0) includes a 'Spec close-out' bullet immediately after 'Artifacts' in every generated `## claude-tweaks Pipeline` section; CLAUDE.md's copy of this section omits it entirely. `specs/` in this repo currently holds one file, so the discipline this bullet establishes (delete after shipping, don't accumulate a permanent index) is directly applicable, not dead weight.

## Deliverables

**Current:**
```
**Artifacts:** design doc (one file, phases = `## Phase N` sections) → spec (one per work unit, via `/claude-tweaks:specify`) → `/claude-tweaks:flow`. No multi-phase plan files (`*-P1.md`, `*-P2.md`, …); a single plan per spec via `/superpowers:writing-plans`, stopped before its execution-choice offer, is expected and normal.
```

**Proposed:**
```
**Artifacts:** design doc (one file, phases = `## Phase N` sections) → spec (one per work unit, via `/claude-tweaks:specify`) → `/claude-tweaks:flow`. No multi-phase plan files (`*-P1.md`, `*-P2.md`, …); a single plan per spec via `/superpowers:writing-plans`, stopped before its execution-choice offer, is expected and normal.

**Spec close-out:** `specs/` is a working directory, not a permanent historical index — once a spec ships and is verified, promote any durable reference content to `docs/reference/*.md` or a skill, repoint by-number citations elsewhere in the repo to the closing commit or PR, then delete the spec file. A permanent tracker file (e.g. `specs/INDEX.md`) is an anti-pattern here, not a convention to preserve.
```

## Acceptance Criteria

CLAUDE.md's `## claude-tweaks Pipeline` section is missing the 'Spec close-out' convention that the currently installed claude-tweaks v6.120.0 plugin's own `claude-md-template.md` mandates for every generated CLAUDE.md, and this repo actively uses `specs/` (one file present) so the missing convention is not merely theoretical.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

Found during a pre-release whole-branch review of `plugin/bin/lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.js`
— all three confirmed still true at this shaping pass:

- **Read-back race** (~line 400): post-write verification (#2073) re-reads immediately with no
  retry/backoff (`if (!verifyClaimLanded(deps, repoSlug, issue, opts.runId, knownTip))`). On the
  contents-API transport `knownTip` is `null`, so the read-back hits GitHub's
  eventually-consistent contents API and can legitimately return the pre-write blob — a spurious
  exit 5 on a claim that actually landed. The file's own header already warns against
  eventually-consistent GitHub reads elsewhere.
- **Claim leak on abort** (~line 227, confirmed): `abort()` releases only `claimedThisRun`
  (`releaseClaimedThisRun(deps, repoSlug, opts.runId, claimedThisRun)`). `stopOrSkip(issue,
  'unverified', 'unverified', 5, {})` runs (confirmed, ~line 401) *before* the target is pushed
  onto `claimedThisRun` (the `claimedThisRun.push(issue)` call is one line after the verification
  check), so a target whose claim genuinely landed (just couldn't be verified back) leaks until
  TTL expiry with no `bot:in-progress` marker making it visible.
- **Stale doc comment** (~line 225, confirmed): `abort()`'s comment still enumerates only exit
  codes 3 and 4 ("`exitCode` is 3 for a `contested`/`inFlight` envelope, 4 for a `transient`
  one") — exit 5 (`unverified`) was added without updating it.

## Deliverables

- Add a bounded retry/backoff to the post-write read-back verification when `knownTip` is `null`,
  before declaring exit 5.
- Release (or otherwise make visible) the `unverified` target's claim on abort, not just
  `claimedThisRun`.
- Update `abort()`'s doc comment to include exit 5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A simulated eventually-consistent stale read on the contents-API path no longer produces a
  spurious exit 5 within the retry window.
- An aborted run with an `unverified` target leaves that claim in a state a later run can
  detect/reclaim before TTL, not silently leaked.
- `abort()`'s doc comment lists exit codes 3, 4, and 5.
- `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

For the read-back race: wrap the `verifyClaimLanded` call (~line 400) in a small bounded
retry loop (a few attempts with a short backoff) specifically for the `knownTip === null` case —
the git-CAS path (`knownTip` set) already has a real tip to compare against and doesn't need
this, since a git-CAS success is immediately consistent. Only declare exit 5 after the retry
window is exhausted. For the claim leak: capture the `unverified` issue's claim state (the
context `verifyClaimLanded` already had before failing) and pass it to `abort()` so it can be
released or explicitly flagged alongside `claimedThisRun`'s own release — the goal is that a
genuinely-landed-but-unverified claim doesn't sit invisible until TTL; releasing it (so a later
run can pick it up cleanly) is the safer default over leaving it silently held. Update the
`abort()` doc comment in the same change.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.js` — the read-back retry (~line 400), the claim
  leak fix (~line 227, `abort()` and the `unverified` stop path), and the doc comment update

## Gotchas

- The retry must be scoped to the `knownTip === null` (contents-API) path only — the git-CAS
  path's `knownTip`-based verification is already immediately consistent and doesn't need
  (or benefit from) a retry; adding one there would just slow down every claim for no
  correctness gain.
- Releasing an `unverified` claim on abort must not race with the claim that write actually
  produced — verify the release targets the same claim identity (`repoSlug`, `issue`, `opts.runId`)
  the write itself used, so a genuinely different run's claim on the same issue is never touched.

## Original request

## Current State
Found during a pre-release whole-branch review of `plugin/bin/lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.js`:

- **Read-back race** (~line 400): post-write verification (#2073) re-reads immediately with no retry/backoff. On the contents-API transport `knownTip` is `null`, so the read-back hits GitHub's eventually-consistent contents API and can legitimately return the pre-write blob — a spurious exit 5 on a claim that actually landed. The file's own header already warns against eventually-consistent GitHub reads elsewhere.
- **Claim leak on abort** (~line 227): `abort()` releases only `claimedThisRun`. `stopOrSkip(issue, 'unverified', 'unverified', 5, {})` runs *before* the target is pushed onto `claimedThisRun` (line ~405), so a target whose claim genuinely landed (just couldn't be verified back) leaks until TTL expiry with no `bot:in-progress` marker making it visible.
- **Stale doc comment** (~line 225): `abort()`'s comment still enumerates only exit codes 3 and 4; exit 5 (`unverified`) was added without updating it.

## Deliverables
- Add a bounded retry/backoff to the post-write read-back verification when `knownTip` is `null`, before declaring exit 5.
- Release (or otherwise make visible) the `unverified` target's claim on abort, not just `claimedThisRun`.
- Update `abort()`'s doc comment to include exit 5.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A simulated eventually-consistent stale read on the contents-API path no longer produces a spurious exit 5 within the retry window.
- An aborted run with an `unverified` target leaves that claim in a state a later run can detect/reclaim before TTL, not silently leaked.

# Reflect — staged finding 2

**Category:** tangential

Origin: reflect full mode from #1875
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`dispatch/mcp-transport.md` already documents, as an accepted gap, that `bin/resolve-linked-prs.js`
(the #1224 open-linked-PR exclusion) has no confirmed MCP mapping and fails open (no exclusions)
when `gh` is absent. This run hit that gap for real, not hypothetically: of the 27 candidates in
the eligible queue, record #1594 already had an open PR (#1908, "Fixes #1594") that the automated
check could not detect on this transport. It was caught only because the dispatching session
independently ran a manual, targeted subagent scan of open PR bodies/titles for closing-keyword
references before finalizing the group selection — a step the documented protocol does not
actually specify or require anywhere. Without that improvised check, #1594 could have been
re-dispatched to a second build in parallel with the already-open PR #1908, producing conflicting
work on the same record.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Treat this as evidence for prioritizing a real MCP mapping for the #1224 check (a batched
      equivalent of `closedByPullRequestsReferences`, or an open-PR title/body scan folded
      directly into `queue-pull-script.md`'s MCP branch) rather than leaving it "accepted for now"
      indefinitely.
- [ ] Until a real mapping exists, consider making the manual verification this run improvised a
      documented, required step in `dispatch/mcp-transport.md`'s Step 2 section for the `gh`-absent
      path, so a future firing doesn't have to independently rediscover the same gap and the same
      workaround.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Either the #1224 check gets a real MCP mapping, or the manual verification workaround is
   promoted from this run's improvisation to a documented, required step for the `gh`-absent
   transport.

_Filed by `reflect` via specShapedBody._

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:build` Common Step 2 executes plans via `/superpowers:subagent-driven-development`, whose own Finish step deletes the plan's SDD workspace (`.superpowers/sdd/{plan}/`) once the final review is clean — including `progress.md`, where SDD convention ledgers deferred-minor review findings. claude-tweaks' wrap-up reads only the run ledger (`docs/plans/*-ledger.md`), so any observation ledgered solely in the SDD workspace is structurally lost at the seam. Observed in run 2026-08-20T154419-spec-1076: a scoped re-review's out-of-scope observation survived only because a later hindsight pass happened to re-surface it.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` Common Step 2 (or the SDD invocation instruction it composes) directs the controller to copy any surviving SDD deferred-minor / parked-finding ledger lines into the run ledger (phase `build/*`, status `deferred` or `observation`) before the SDD workspace is deleted.
- [ ] The instruction names the source (`{workspace}/progress.md` lines matching `minor (deferred)` / `parked`) and the destination table's column shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After a `/build` run whose SDD pass recorded at least one deferred minor, the run ledger contains those lines and the SDD workspace is deleted — verifiable by inspecting `docs/plans/{run}-ledger.md` post-build.
2. A conformance check (or the existing suite pattern) pins the instruction's presence in `build/SKILL.md`.

Origin: ledger resolve gate

Defer-reason: blocked-dependency

## Current State

Record #1302 built the WEBHOOK-TRIGGER mode (`plugin/skills/routine/webhook-trigger.md`), the `webhook_triggers` schema field, the filter grammar, and both preconditions -- all documented from `create_webhook_trigger`'s own tool description, since `RemoteTrigger` was confirmed unavailable via `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` in that build session. This is the 4th consecutive session (2026-08-23 x2, 2026-08-26, 2026-09-05) to confirm the same unavailability. AC2 ("verified against a real (or explicitly documented dry-run) call") remains unmet: the request/response shape has never actually been confirmed against a live `create_webhook_trigger` call.

A prior follow-up for this same gap, #1485, was filed and closed on 2026-08-31 -- but the closing commit (`e0d4aded`, "[fast-lane] Dispatch-queue, worktree-guard, reconcile, and process-hygiene fixes (19 records)") bundled 19 unrelated record numbers via `Fixes #N` and contains no work touching `webhook-trigger.md`, `RemoteTrigger`, or live-call verification. #1485 appears to have been swept into an unrelated batch closure rather than substantively resolved -- its own acceptance criterion (a live or explicit-dry-run `create_webhook_trigger` call) was never actually satisfied. This record exists so the gap is not lost a second time to the same failure mode; whoever picks this up should close it only against real evidence of a live (or explicit dry-run) call, not a batch commit that doesn't mention the file.

## Deliverables

- Re-run `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` in a session where the tool may be reachable -- 4 consecutive interactive-session misses is a strong signal worth testing in a different session type (cloud/routine) if one becomes available.
- Once reachable, call `create_webhook_trigger` against a real (or an explicit, logged dry-run) routine and record its actual required fields, response shape, and any App-not-installed error text.
- Diff the actual response against what `plugin/skills/routine/webhook-trigger.md` currently documents (Step 5's assembled body, the `routine_trigger_id` field, the App-not-installed error detection) and correct any mismatch.
- Before closing, verify the closing commit/PR actually touches `webhook-trigger.md` or names the live-verification evidence directly -- do not let this close via an unrelated batch sweep the way #1485 did.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A live (or explicit dry-run) `create_webhook_trigger` call has been made and its actual request/response shape is confirmed to match (or has been corrected to match) `plugin/skills/routine/webhook-trigger.md`.
- The closing commit or PR description names this evidence directly (a transcript excerpt, a diff to `webhook-trigger.md`, or an explicit "confirmed matching, no changes needed" note) rather than a bare `Fixes #N` in an unrelated batch.

## Technical Approach

Start with `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` in whichever session type is available at build time. If reachable, make one real or explicit-dry-run `create_webhook_trigger` call and capture its actual request/response shape verbatim before touching the docs. Then diff that captured shape against `webhook-trigger.md`'s current documentation section by section (assembled body, `routine_trigger_id`, App-not-installed error detection) and correct only what actually differs.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/routine/webhook-trigger.md` -- the documented request/response shape to verify and correct

## Gotchas

- If `RemoteTrigger`/`create_webhook_trigger` is still unreachable in whatever session builds this record, do not fabricate a "verified" result and do not close this record -- report the continued unavailability plainly (a 5th consecutive miss is itself a useful data point) and leave it open.
- Do not let this close via a bulk/batch commit that references this issue number without actually touching the files above -- that is exactly how #1485 was lost.

Surface: backend

## Current State

Record #649 added `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s fan-out single-assistant-message-rule
sentence and per-site citations (AC1, fully test-pinned in `tests/subagent-contract-clauses.test.js`,
18/18 passing). AC2 — "A `/specify` red-team over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues launches its
personas in ≤ (number of sub-issues) assistant messages, verified in the transcript by `Agent`
tool_use blocks sharing a message id" — is a live-behavior criterion that cannot be verified by a
static `node --test` assertion; it can only be confirmed by observing an actual future `/specify`
decomposition run's transcript.

## Deliverables

Confirm, at the next `/specify` decomposition run over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues, that
persona dispatch actually batches into ≤N assistant messages per `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s
fan-out single-assistant-message rule and `red-team.md`'s per-sub-issue batching unit. Record the
observation (transcript excerpt or note) against this item, or file a defect against
`red-team.md`'s dispatch prose if it does not.

## Acceptance Criteria

A `/specify` run over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues is observed; its persona `Agent` tool_use
calls are confirmed (via transcript `tool_use` block message-id grouping) to arrive in ≤ (number of
sub-issues) assistant messages.

## Technical Approach

Wait for (or trigger) a `/claude-tweaks:specify` decomposition-mode run that produces 2 or more
`ceremony:standard` sub-issue records — `ceremony-check` (`assess-agent-autonomy/ceremony-check.md`)
resolves the tier per sub-issue during that run's own Step 3, so the tier isn't knowable until the
run happens. Once such a run occurs, inspect that session's stored transcript for the Step 5
red-team dispatch (`specify/red-team.md`'s Parallel dispatch section): locate the `Agent` tool_use
blocks for each dispatched persona and group them by the assistant message id each block belongs
to. Confirm the number of distinct assistant message ids covering all persona dispatches for a
given sub-issue is ≤ the number of sub-issues in that batch. Use the same read-only transcript
inspection method `transcript-payload-verification` documents for reading this session's own
locally-stored transcript, rather than instrumenting or modifying `red-team.md` itself.

If the count exceeds the bound, file a defect issue against `red-team.md`'s dispatch prose
(quoting the transcript grouping that violates the rule) instead of editing the file directly from
this record — this record's own deliverable is the observation, not the fix.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/specify/red-team.md` — the per-sub-issue persona dispatch procedure being observed
- `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` — the fan-out single-assistant-message rule this observation verifies compliance with
- `tests/subagent-contract-clauses.test.js` — AC1's existing static test coverage (unaffected by this record)

## Gotchas

- This record's acceptance criterion depends on an external event (a live `/specify` decomposition
  run over 2+ `ceremony:standard` sub-issues happening) that this record cannot itself trigger on a
  fixed schedule — it may sit open for some time until a qualifying run occurs naturally, or until
  someone deliberately runs one to close it out.
- A qualifying run must be observed via its own transcript at the time it happens; this record
  cannot be resolved from historical data if no already-completed run's transcript is still
  available.

## Original request

Surface: backend

## Current State
`captureDebugPayload` (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js:1633`) is env-gated (`CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE`) diagnostic instrumentation wired directly into `run()` — the general hook dispatcher invoked on every covered tool call — added by #1501 to chase a repro-resistant #989 investigation. #1501's own investigation found the actual cause without it (a fresh worktree's `@{u}` inherited `origin/main`), and #1860/PR #1874 (merged 2026-09-05) fixed `hasNoUpstreamYet` for that case with regression tests covering the inherited-upstream shape. The harness gap the instrumentation was added to diagnose is closed at the test level. Nothing in the repo reads the capture file, and no other open record cites `CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE`. A maintainer has decided (this record's own resolution, 2026-09-13) to remove the instrumentation rather than keep it as permanent tooling.

## Deliverables
- Remove `captureDebugPayload(ctx)` (function definition, its header comment block, and its call site in `run()`) from `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`.
- Remove the three `CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE` tests and their preceding comment block from `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `captureDebugPayload`'s function definition, its header comment (the `#1501: env-gated debug capture...` block), and its `captureDebugPayload(ctx);` call inside `run()` no longer exist in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`.
- [ ] The three `CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE` tests (`unset by default, no file is written`; `when set, appends one JSON line per call...`; `an unwritable target never breaks the real gate call`) and their preceding `#1501` comment no longer exist in `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js`.
- [ ] `grep -rn "captureDebugPayload\|CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE" plugin/ tests/` returns no results.
- [ ] Full `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach
Delete the `captureDebugPayload` function (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`, currently ~lines 1621-1646 including its header comment) and its call site inside `run()` (currently the `captureDebugPayload(ctx);` statement at the top of `run()`, ~line 1649) — `run()`'s remaining body is unaffected; it already builds `indeterminateTargets`/`warnings` and calls `runInner` immediately after.

Delete the corresponding test block in `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js` (currently ~lines 1127-1176: the `#1501` comment plus all three `CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE` tests) — the surrounding tests (the preceding block and the following `#1967` git-stash test) are unaffected and need no renumbering.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — remove `captureDebugPayload` function, its header comment, and its call in `run()`
- `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js` — remove the three `CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE` tests and their preceding comment

## Gotchas
- `run()` calls `captureDebugPayload(ctx)` unconditionally as its first statement — confirmed only one call site and one definition exist in the repo (`grep -rn "captureDebugPayload\|CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE"` against `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` and `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js`) before removing either.
- Pure removal with no behavior change for any caller — `CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE` was already a no-op unless the env var was explicitly set for a deliberate capture session, so no production behavior depends on it.

## Original request

pre-tool-use.js: captureDebugPayload is permanent scaffolding in the production hook dispatcher

## Current State
`captureDebugPayload` (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`, ~line 1409) — permanent, env-gated (`CT_HOOKS_DEBUG_CAPTURE`) diagnostic instrumentation added to chase one repro-resistant #989 bug — is wired directly into `run()`, the general hook dispatcher invoked on every covered tool call, rather than the actual ctx-field gap (between synthetic test payloads and live invocations) being closed in the test harness. Low runtime cost when unset, but sets a precedent for future "repro doesn't match" investigations to keep accumulating env-gated capture hooks in the production dispatcher rather than fixing the harness gap that necessitated it.

## Deliverables
Either (a) close the actual ctx-field gap in the test harness so synthetic payloads match live invocations and remove `captureDebugPayload` from `run()`, or (b) make a deliberate call to keep it as permanent tooling and document why in place of the current "added to chase one bug" framing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A decision is made and recorded: remove captureDebugPayload (harness gap closed) or keep it deliberately (comment updated to reflect permanent-tooling intent).
- [ ] Full `npm test` passes.

Defer-reason: needs-human-decision — whether to invest in closing the harness gap vs. keep the instrumentation is a product/maintainer call, not a mechanical fix; found by the pre-v6.112.0 whole-branch review.

## Current State

Found during a pre-release whole-branch review. #2019 split `_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`'s
Resolution-order content out into a new `_shared/run-dir-resolution.md`, and migrated most
citers, but two gaps remain — both confirmed still present at this shaping pass:

- `plugin/skills/research/verify-mode.md` (confirmed, lines ~124 and ~184) still cites
  `pipeline-run-dir.md` for content that moved: "not on the standalone-auto allowlist in
  `skills/_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`" (now `run-dir-resolution.md` step 4) and
  "`_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`'s most-recent-matching-directory fallback" (now step 2). Every
  other named citer (`/capture`, `tidy/step-6-auto.md`, `flow/materialize.md`,
  `_shared/auto-decision-log.md`, `sweep/SKILL.md`) was migrated.
- `_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md` itself (confirmed, lines ~31, 33) has two internal references
  that now dangle: "step 4's standalone-auto-fallback shape" and "when the caller is on the
  standalone-auto allowlist above" — neither step 4 nor the allowlist lives in this file any
  more (both moved to `run-dir-resolution.md:14-19`). This file's remaining sections are the CLI
  reference, Anchoring, and the worktree-local `--run` fallback.

## Deliverables

- Retarget `research/verify-mode.md`'s two citations to `run-dir-resolution.md`.
- Fix `pipeline-run-dir.md`'s two dangling internal self-references to point at the correct
  file/step now that the content moved out.

## Acceptance Criteria

Neither file references content by a step number or "above"/"below" pointer that no longer
resolves in the cited location.

## Technical Approach

Four targeted text edits, no logic change:

1. `research/verify-mode.md` (~line 124): change "not on the standalone-auto allowlist in
   `skills/_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`" to cite `_shared/run-dir-resolution.md`'s step 4
   allowlist instead.
2. `research/verify-mode.md` (~line 184): change "`_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`'s
   most-recent-matching-directory fallback" to cite `_shared/run-dir-resolution.md`'s step 2

3. `pipeline-run-dir.md` (~line 31): change "step 4's standalone-auto-fallback shape" to name
